stage3.sig: WEB to DB direct - microsegmentation bypass

summary.thesis_claim: Proposed agent escalates with kill-chain context (higher confidence, correlation markers present); SOAR correctly mitigates on SID match but cannot escalate, correlate across stages, or distinguish cold vs. sequence.

reasoning: Flow violates explicit microsegmentation policy: WEB zone (10.1.100.10) → DB-OLTP zone (10.1.200.10:5432) is DENY in policy matrix. This is a hard architectural boundary - WEB tier must proxy through APP-GW → APP-CORE → DB-OLTP chain.

Flow is absent from production baselines: Legitimate WEB outbound is only to APP-GW (10.3.100.10:8080). DB-OLTP only accepts inbound from APP-CORE, WORKER, MGT, MONITORING. Direct WEB→DB has zero legitimate runtime use case.

Source is a repeat offender: 10.1.100.10 has 36 prior SID 9000001 incidents (100% enforcement rate), trust score 0.39, runtime reputation 0.00 (very_low) with 11 true positives in last hour. This is not a first-time anomaly.

Multi-SID kill-chain signal: Recent alert sequence shows 9000001, 9000001, 9000901, 9000905, 9000002 - indicating active campaign progression across lateral movement stages, not isolated misconfiguration.

MITRE T1021/TA0008 classification: Suricata SID 9000001 explicitly maps to Remote Services lateral movement technique. The TCP SYN to PostgreSQL port (5432) matches the attack pattern of credential stuffing or direct connection attempt.

Targeted block preserves legitimate traffic: Dropping only 10.1.100.10→10.1.200.10:5432 maintains web-to-appgw-proxy (critical) while stopping the violation. Full-source block would cause user-facing outage.

Confidence calibrated at 0.95: Matches threat pattern cross_zone_violation_web_to_db with confidence anchor 0.95. No false-positive scenarios apply (no migration window, no MGT involvement, no monitoring baseline).

hypotheses.name: Lateral movement from compromised web-01
hypotheses.description: Lateral movement from compromised web-01 (probability=0.95) — WEB host attempting direct DB access to bypass application chain. Evidence: SID 9000001 trigger, policy violation (WEB→DB=DENY), not in baseline, repeat offender with 36 prior exact-SID incidents. Counter: None significant - no legitimate use case for WEB→DB direct.

hypotheses.name: Misconfigured monitoring tool
hypotheses.description: Misconfigured monitoring tool (probability=0.03) — Monitoring agent incorrectly configured to probe DB from web tier. Evidence: None - no monitoring baseline includes WEB→DB. Counter: Monitoring zone is separate (10.4.200.0/24) and would originate from MON, not WEB.

hypotheses.name: Pre-announced DB migration script
hypotheses.description: Pre-announced DB migration script (probability=0.02) — Emergency maintenance script run from WEB host. Evidence: None - no change-window notification, no MGT involvement. Counter: DB migrations should originate from MGT zone per compliance policy.
